correctness.rationale: The weighted U-statistic and product-measure argument proves the selected tuple limit almost surely; simplex substitution gives the claimed Dirichlet parameters; a Voronoi integral and uniform empirical Wasserstein convergence prove normalized cost and optimum; Dirichlet rising-factorial moments yield the exact variance and uniform-sampling gap (checked symbolically and rationally); the published conditional expected-cost <=2k OPT bound yields uniform integrability for expected ratios; gamma CLT/delta method gives asymptotic variance 3/4. All the quantifiers and endpoint cases are treated for k>=2. Standalone verification executed 277 finite checks; it is supplemental, not used as a proof of convergence.

value.rationale: This is a stochastic evaluation of an actively studied nontrivial mechanism with exact all-k asymptotic mean, full selected-spacing law, nonzero cost variance, strict benchmark comparison, and a Gaussian second-scale result. The quantitative gap between typical performance (near 3/2) and worst-case 2k is meaningful for mechanism assessment. The result is not merely a routine substitution or re-labeling, since it proves conditional random-subset convergence and a distinct high-k fluctuation theorem.
